a) the proposed algorithms for affine cameras are the most accurate methods for 3D reconstruction in the presence of missing data b) they are also applicable to projective cameras and c) they have a lower complexity than existing methods.

a) linear algorithms for 3D reconstruction of multiple views are possible b) they are more efficient than existing methods c) they are more robust than existing methods d) they are applicable to a wide range of real world data.

a) a unified treatment of affine and perspective cameras is possible in a projective camera model, and that b) linear multi view reconstruction from multiple views of points with missing data can be done efficiently and robustly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of reconstructing 3D scenes from 2D images.
3D reconstruction in a projective geometry setting from multiple views of multiple points.
3D reconstruction methods for multi view images which are able to deal with missing data, which is often the case in real world applications, and which are computationally efficient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented algorithms perform better than the factorization methods for all the experiments.
for most cases the proposed algorithms are more robust than existing ones and that the proposed methods are also faster and more flexible.
the presented algorithms are the most efficient and accurate methods for general multi view reconstruction with missing data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

linear multi view reconstruction with missing data can be done with a single linear system of equations, and that it is possible to compute the 3D structure and the motion of multiple cameras from only three points that are visible in all views, and that it works even in the case of projectively distorted views.
the proposed methods are the first to handle missing data in general affine and projectives views.
we can reconstruct 3D points from 2D data with missing points, and we can reconstruct 2D points from 3D data with missing views.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the new methods are much more flexible and robust than previous approaches and that they are able to handle missing data much more efficiently.
it is possible to compute camera and scene parameters from linear systems of equations, which is much more efficient than factorization methods.
linear methods are not only fast but also robust and can compete with nonlinear methods in terms of accuracy.
